## Upgrading from 0.10

Fondu and create-fondu share version 0.11.0. Existing apps update `fondu`; use the matching create-fondu version
for new apps. Rebuild and deploy the client and server together: the generated page-data URLs belong to their build,
not to an application API to hard-code or keep across deployments.

### Navigation

The client now uses the History API instead of the Navigation API. Plain links and forms remain the way to navigate;
apps that integrated with Navigation API events should review that integration. No separate client route
configuration is needed.

Back and Forward show a kept page immediately, at its previous scroll position, then ask the server for the current
page. Kept pages live in memory only and are forgotten when a form is submitted. Flash messages are not replayed
from kept pages. A document reload restores its saved position when available, including on pages using
`withoutSsr()` and pages scrolled away from a fragment target. `reload()` still asks for the current page's props
without resetting its state or scroll position.

Client render errors now use the app's error page. Form encodings and line breaks follow native submissions;
malformed multipart bodies return 400, and repeated nested fields retain their values.

See [Pages and props](https://fondu.dev/docs/pages) and [Forms and validation](https://fondu.dev/docs/forms).

### Prerendering and index URLs

Page-data URLs distinguish directory indexes from parameter values such as `index` and `~index`, including their
percent-encoded spellings. Treat these URLs as framework-generated; continue to link to the page's own URL.

With the current static-file layout, a URL whose final decoded path segment is exactly `index` and which has no
trailing slash cannot be prerendered: its HTML file would be its directory's `index.html`. The build now fails with
the route and URL instead of allowing that ambiguity. Exclude those URLs from the `prerender` list; they can still
be rendered dynamically, subject to the Cloudflare limitation below.

This does not prohibit `index.tsx` files mapping to `/` or `/blog`, names such as `/blog/my-index`, or a canonical
trailing-slash URL such as `/blog/index/`.

On Cloudflare, the build merges `/index` and `/*/index` into the generated `assets.run_worker_first` list, or keeps an
existing `true`, so literal index-ending paths reach their routes rather than Static Assets' directory redirects.
Bun and Node likewise leave those document requests to their routes instead of reading the directory's static file.

### Known Cloudflare limitation

In an assets-first deployment, a percent-encoded document path such as `/%69ndex` can still be redirected to `/`
before reaching the Worker. The selective Worker-first patterns match the raw path, while Static Assets recognize
the decoded `index`. Client navigation can reach the intended page even when the direct document request is
redirected. Bun and Node do not have this asset-layer limitation.

A Worker-first design with explicit asset delegation can handle those requests, but switching
`run_worker_first: true` alone is not a drop-in workaround: the Worker must also handle or delegate static asset
requests. See [Static pages](https://fondu.dev/docs/static-pages#cloudflare-routing) for the restriction and routing
trade-off.

### Non-interactive app creation

create-fondu now requires an explicit `--target bun|cloudflare|node` with `--yes` or without a terminal, rather than
opening a prompt that cannot be answered. For example:

```sh
bun create fondu@0.11.0 my-app --target node --yes
```

When the target is given but the directory is omitted in a non-interactive invocation, it creates `my-app`.
